subject: Post-call: ACME TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@acmecorp.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: ACME TCO recap & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful conversation. Quick recap of what we heard, which we'll use to scope the pricing/PoC:

Summary of pain points:
- Token economics at scale: current vendor costs are spiking with >1B tokens/mo and variable batching leads to unpredictable costs.
- Latency & tail spikes during peak ingestion windows (batching strategy inconsistent).
- Concerns about embedding cost when doing semantic search for support docs.

Goals you shared:
- Reduce per-inference cost by ~3x (short term) while keeping p95 latency under 250ms for interactive flows.
- Centralize model serving to avoid multiple duplicate deployments across teams.
- Rollout a 6-month plan with measurable ROI and clear procurement path.

Key levers we discussed (high-level):
- Batching & dynamic micro-batching: higher effective throughput with minimal latency impact for non-real-time flows.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context to reduce repeated attention compute.
- Quantization to int8/4 and model variant selection for cost vs quality tradeoffs.
- Intelligent routing: route non-critical requests to cheaper model variants or batchers.
- Dedicated capacity option for predictable throughput and committed pricing.

Ballpark TCO framing (very rough, see attached spreadsheet for details):
- Your current: ~1.0B tokens/mo -> external vendor baseline ~$28k / 1M tokens (example) -> monthly token spend ~$28k * 1000 = $28M (we'll detail lines in sheet).
- Redwood baseline (after batching + caching + quantization): expected 3.0–4.0x reduction in token compute cost before reserved discounts.
- Example: per 1M tokens effective cost after optimizations: $6–9 (varies by model/quality); embeddings add ~20–30% depending on use.

Next steps we recommend:
1) I attached a populated TCO model (ACME_TCO_model.xlsx) with assumptions from today — please review and flag any numbers that need updates.
2) Rafael (cc'd) to run a focused pricing deep dive with your engineering and finance teams to map infrastructure vs software line items.
3) Laura (cc'd) to coordinate procurement readiness (SOC2 / data retention) and initial SOW/terms.
4) Proposed PoC: 6 weeks focused on a single high-traffic endpoint (dedicated capacity trial + caching) — output: measured cost delta and latency p95.

Proposed time for the deep-dive: Wed 3/3 or Thu 3/4 (Rafael + Laura + Alex/engineering). Let me know what works.

Attachments:
- ACME_TCO_model.xlsx (spreadsheet with token assumptions & cost lines)
- redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (pricing tiers + dedicated commit options)

If you want a one-pager ROI summary I can send a 1-page with the 6-month savings and payback timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@acmecorp.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME TCO recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid summary. A couple quick clarifications before we dive into the spreadsheet:
- Our forecasting constraint: we have ~USD 250,000 allocated for LLM infra (model serving + embeddings) for the next 6 months. Can you show a path that stays within that envelope (or a clear ask if extra commit is required for the expected savings)?
- Please separate the TCO rows for model serving compute vs embedding costs vs storage/monitoring so finance can map to their budgets.
- Procurement will need SOC2 + data retention policy documented before any dedicated commit.

Happy to join Wed 3/3 at 10am PT for the deep-dive if Rafael and Laura can make it. Priya from procurement will join for the compliance checklist.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Products, ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@acmecorp.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME TCO recap & next steps

Appreciate the context, Alex — good note on separating lines. I've updated the attached ACME_TCO_model.xlsx to present three tabs: "Serving", "Embeddings", "Infra & Ops" with line-item assumptions (requests per second, average tokens per request, cache hit rate, batch size, quantization savings).

Quick highlights from the updated model (assumptions are adjustable):
- Baseline assumptions: 1.0B tokens/mo, cache hit 18%, average batch efficiency reduces compute by ~22% for non-real-time flows.
- With conservative batching (avg effective batch size 6) + prefix caching 25% hit, plus mixed quantization strategy (int8 for >=75% of traffic), we see an estimated monthly cost of ~$180k (total infra + embeddings + ops) — within your $250k envelope and leaves headroom for growth.
- If you opt for a 6-12 month reserved commit on Dedicated capacity we can push effective cost down to ~$120k/mo and guarantee throughput and latency SLOs. That tradeoff requires an initial commit — Rafael can walk through commit levels and discounts.
- ROI: with reserved commit option the estimated payback is ~3–4 months vs current spend (assuming usage stability).

Attachments in this message: ACME_TCO_model.xlsx (detailed assumptions), redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (tiered pricing + reserved commit levels).

Proposed meeting: Wed 3/3 at 10:00am PT — Rafael + Laura joining to cover engineering and procurement. Draft agenda:
1) Review TCO tabs & assumptions (15m)
2) Rafael: Dedicated pricing and commit levels (15m)
3) Laura: Compliance checklist & procurement timeline (10m)
4) Next steps / PoC scope (10m)

If that works I'll calendar invite — Rafael, Laura, feel free to edit.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment stubs:
- ACME_TCO_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com, rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME TCO recap & next steps

Thanks — this looks promising. A few procurement items to kick off:
- Please share your standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) + typical SOW template and any initial pricing exhibits so procurement can review.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II report and a documented data retention & deletion policy for the PoC.
- For the dedicated commit option, procurement needs a clear minimum commit and a cancellation/exit clause to evaluate risk.

If you can drop the MSA and SOC2 link before the deep-dive that would speed things up. Wed 3/3 at 10am PT works for me.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Procurement Lead, ACME Corp
priya@acmecorp.com
